 Govt raises LPG price 5.27pc for November
 Business 
 By   Israr Khan 
 November 01, 2026 
 Gas cylinder vendors working at a shop. — APP/File ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s oil and gas regulator has raised liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices by 5.27 per cent for November, adding Rs174 to the cost of a standard household cylinder, as higher LPG prices put another burden on consumers who rely on the fuel for cooking.
 The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) set the consumer price at Rs294.1 per kilogram from Sunday, up from Rs279.3 in October, according to its latest notification.
 The price of an 11.8-kilogram household cylinder will rise to Rs3,470, from Rs3,296 previously. The increase means households will pay about Rs174 more for the same cylinder.
 The price of a 45.4-kg commercial cylinder will rise by Rs669 to Rs13,351, increasing costs for businesses that use LPG as a cooking or heating fuel.
 Notably, last month too, the government had increased its prices by 8.0 per cent or 244/cylinder for October.
 The repeated increases are particularly significant for lower-income households and consumers in areas without access to piped natural gas, where LPG is widely used as an alternative cooking fuel.
 Taxes and other charges account for a sizeable portion of the regulated price. Ogra’s pricing structure includes a petroleum levy of Rs4,669 per tonne and GST of Rs38,559 per tonne.
 An additional 18 per cent GST of Rs6,300 is imposed on marketing, distribution and transportation margins, bringing total margin-related charges to about Rs35,000 per tonne.
